title: Aflibercept for clinically significant diabetic macular edema: 12-month results in daily clinical practice

license.statement: Dove Medical Press licence incorporating CC BY-NC 3.0 (unported) (article <license>); non-commercial, so private

condition: Clinically significant diabetic macular edema, anti-VEGF naive; prospective open-label single-centre observational study in daily practice (Plasencia, Spain, enrolment March 2015 to March 2016), 29 eyes of 15 patients followed 12 months

groups.agent: aflibercept 2 mg/0.05 mL (Eylea), five loading doses every 4 weeks then a fixed dose every 8 weeks
groups.description: All study eyes (29 eyes of 15 patients)

series.notes: Methods: 'central subfield macular thickness' by SD-OCT (Cirrus HD-OCT); tables and Abstract call it central macular thickness; mean (SD); visits at the times stated in the Methods and Table 2 labels (visit 2 at 5 months after the five loading doses, then 7, 9 and 12 months); all 29 eyes followed for 12 months (Results); the Abstract's baseline SD differs from Table 2, Table 2 cited

exclusions.what: Table 2 95% CI column (C3) and CI of the difference (C5)
exclusions.reason: confidence-interval bounds are not admissible as values
changes from baseline of the same eyes duplicate the absolute series; the absolute series is used
differences between follow-up visits are not a series from baseline

notes: Prior treatment: anti-VEGF naive per the Methods; prior laser is not stated
Laser photocoagulation was allowed by protocol for a decrease in BCVA; the Results report no vision loss and no other treatment during the study
Both eyes of most patients are included (29 eyes of 15 patients)
